a feedforward deep convolutional neural network can be used to model affordance-related activity in scene-selective visual areas, and the computations that support these representations are consistent with the known sensory functions of these areas.
a deep convolutional neural network can be used to gain insights into cortical computations by mapping the sensory functions of visual cortex onto a fully quantitative computational model.

a biologically inspired deep convolution neural network can serve as a candidate computational model for affordance-related responses within the occipital-place area, and that the internal operations of this model can be used to understand the visual computations underlying this cortical function.

the computational mechanisms that underlie the perception of affordances.
the development and application of computational models to understand the mechanisms underlying the processing of visual information in the brain.
the computational mechanisms underlying responses to the affordances of visual scenes in the human occipital place-area (OPA).
